reason: The PR changes Trip construction and LocalSearch solution export in the solver engine, removing temporary vectors and a copy during repeated search-state materialization.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: Reducing temporary allocation and copying during trip and solution creation may let the solver execute more search iterations per fixed time budget and find better CVRP solutions.
causal_chain: Trip construction now reuses one load segment per dimension, while LocalSearch moves completed trip vectors into routes; this may lower allocation and copy cost per exported solution without changing the search policy.
structural_trigger: CVRP runs with nonempty routes whose search repeatedly constructs trips and exports local-search solutions.
activation_probe: Count Trip constructor and LocalSearch::exportSolution calls, record allocations or peak RSS, and pair end-to-end solve trajectories.
instance_selection_rule: Use the fixed PyVRP CVRP development, hidden ID, and generated-shift panels selected before observing this PR's effect; retain all instances and seeds.
workload_exposure_plan: Run the pinned pre-PR source and source-only PR patch on the existing CVRP panels with identical budgets, seeds, and independent route verification.
mathematical_risk: A changed load calculation or moved trip vector could produce incorrect route capacity, incomplete search state, or an invalid reported objective.
independent_check_plan: Verify every returned route and objective against the original CVRP instance; compare load and route-cost invariants on targeted constructor cases.
hidden_generalization_plan: Compare paired hidden ID and generated-shift CVRP panels, including convergence, failures, and instance-level regressions at the predeclared budgets.
overlap_review: Compare PR #968 and nearby search-loading changes before treating them as independent task lineages.
resource_risk: Repeating the visits loop per load dimension may trade memory savings for more traversal work on multi-dimensional instances.
